newsitem.title: USA: Wis. ballpark district considering $45 mln of COPs.
newsitem.headline: Wis. ballpark district considering $45 mln of COPs.

text.p: The district overseeing construction of the new Milwaukee Brewers ballpark is leaning toward issuing $45 million of certificates of participation for big ticket leased equipment, finance manager Jim Gultry said Tuesday.
The financing team for the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District is scheduled to discuss alternatives with the district's Finance Committee Wednesday, Gultry said.
The big equipment needs could include scoreboards and motors for the retractable roof, Gultry said.
District representatives will discuss the possibility of operating leases, private placement, conventional financing, tax-exempt bonds and certificates of participation, Gultry said.
But what officials are "leaning toward, and the recommendation I think will come from the Finance Committee," are COPs, Gultry said.
The financing team is not necessarily looking for approval of a proposal Wednesday, Gultry said.
"We would love to get this out of the way," Gultry said. "It has been almost a year since the groundbreaking, so I think it is about time we have how we are going to pay for this done and over with."
The district has already issued $146 million of revenue bonds backed by a 0.1 percent five-county sales tax for the facility now called Miller Park.
